newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbia announces early plans for cable TV network.
newsitem.headline: Serbia announces early plans for cable TV network.

text.p: Serbia announced plans on Friday for a 15-year programme to establish a cable television network, to improve the flow of information to every part of the country.
"Our key aim is to improve flow of information to the most remote rural parts, regardless of who produces the programme," Serbian Construction Minister Branislav Ivkovic told a news conference.
"Development of telecommunications is important in overall development of Serbia and its economy until 2010," he said.
The government is now due to pass legislation, giving more detail on who and under what conditions can invest in creating cable television systems and operate the cable.
Ivkovic said the government would consider concessions to foreign investors, but gave no further detail.

"Any early foreign investment, before the parliament adopts a new telecommunications law (due to be discussed in the parliament early in 1997), would observe existing laws on foreign investment, companies and telecommunications," an information ministry official told Reuters.

Even though the presented paper did not deal with finances, costs are estimated at several hundred million dollars, Milan Topalovic head of the project, said. There were no details on the launch date.
Aleksandar Marincic of the Belgrade School of Electrical Engineering said the project would help improve Serbia and Yugoslavia's links with the rest of the world.
The new cable network would run along other main infrastructure routes, including PTT, electricity and gas networks, reducing installation costs, he said.
"Serbia's system would be a hybrid network, because economic reality over next ten years would not allow for a more desired fibre optic network," Marincic said.

Ideally, fibre optic cable extension would run to every client, but in the case of Serbia, it would only run along main highways, while final distribution would use coaxial cable -- efficient, simple and of sufficient capacity, he said.
The network's hierarchy would be divided into four levels -- national, regional, local and the last one for final distribution.
All cable systems would be designed at full frequency volume of 860 MHz, enabling transmission of dozens of analogue television programmes. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
